# Carlos Asmat

> Robotics engineer who designs, builds and debugs robot hardware and the software that runs on it, from the schematic to the shipped product. Carlos has shipped humanoid behaviors, an autonomous consumer robot, and wearable exoskeletons.

Carlos Asmat works where a part choice on a schematic shows up later as latency, battery life, a certification cycle, or how the robot feels to the person using it. His career spans humanoid interaction robots, autonomous consumer robots, and wearable robotic platforms, from first prototype through production.

At Aldebaran (later SoftBank Robotics), he built the physical and verbal interaction behaviors for the NAO and Pepper humanoid robots and ran their public demonstrations, including for Neil deGrasse Tyson and Buzz Aldrin. At Piaggio Fast Forward, he was the first electrical and software engineer on gita: he designed its electronic architecture for mass production, built the ML pipeline for vision-based person detection and tracking on a Jetson Nano, contributed to the patented self-balancing drive (US 11,613,325), and grew the engineering team to 25.

At Dephy, he leads electrical and software engineering for powered exoskeletons, including the consumer Sidekick and a next-generation platform developed with Nike: controller architecture, field-oriented motor control, IMU and sensor integration, wireless connectivity, telemetry, and ISO 13482 compliance. He presents architecture and roadmap decisions to the board and to partners, and explains trade-offs to engineers and executives in the same terms.

## Site structure

- [Resume](https://asmat.ca/)
- [Blog](https://asmat.ca/blog/)
- [RSS Feed](https://asmat.ca/feed.xml)

## Featured posts

- [Bump it, Bro: Embrace the Limitations](https://asmat.ca/blog/bump-it-bro/) - Designing physical social interactions (fist bumps, hugs, handshakes) for NAO and Pepper robots at Aldebaran. Covers human-robot interaction design under hardware constraints, with demos for Neil deGrasse Tyson, Buzz Aldrin, Tyra Banks, and will.i.am.
- [Sigmoids are the Best!](https://asmat.ca/blog/sigmoids-are-the-best/) - Why hard threshold checks misbehave in code that actuates in the physical world, and how smooth transitions fix them.
- [I Went BanaNAS](https://asmat.ca/blog/i-went-bananas/) - A home server built from a mini PC and a 3D-printed drive enclosure, with ZFS RAIDZ2 and an ESP32-S3 touch screen front panel written in C with LVGL.
- [Resistance is Futile](https://asmat.ca/blog/resistance-is-futile/) - An EE calculator for the computations used daily at the bench (LED resistors and more), with the math behind each one, built as a dependency-free web component.

## Areas of expertise

- Robot system architecture across electrical hardware, firmware, and software
- Embedded controllers: MCU selection, field-oriented motor control, current sensing, power
- Sensing: IMU, sensor fusion, encoders, capacitive sensing
- Embedded vision and ML pipelines on device (Jetson)
- Wireless connectivity, telemetry, and data infrastructure
- Human-robot interaction (HRI), social robotics, interaction design
- Humanoid robots, autonomous consumer robots, exoskeletons
- Safety standards for personal care robots (ISO 13482)
- C/C++, Python, ROS, FreeRTOS, Linux
- Hiring and leading EE, firmware, and software teams

## Blog

The blog has two sections:

- **Recent posts** (2019+): Current writing on software, robotics, and tools
- **Carlitos' Contraptions Archive** (2006-2013): Restored from the old carlitoscontraptions.com blog, covering personal maker projects, robotics (including the Nao 1337 humanoid robot), electronics, Arduino, and DIY builds
